main_body: A bare, snow-dusted birch-like tree: a tall pale trunk with a branching canopy of dark twigs and small snow patches at the top, and a small snow mound at the base.
top_band: none - the canopy is a sparse web of dark branches with snow flecks; no distinct horizontal top surface. Trunk column from row ~10 down reads only as a vertical pale cylinder.
evidence: The tree is drawn as a flat, near-symmetrical front view. The trunk is a narrow vertical column with a light left side and dark right edge, with no surface visible from above. The branches fan out as thin lines, and the snow flecks are scattered rather than forming a top band. No top band, front edge line or eave shadow is present. This is an organic plant, so it has no obvious flat top surface. Under the strict rules, though, there is no readable top mass sitting over a front face, so it fails.

style.evidence: The reference trees are dense, rounded canopies with 5 or more leaf greens, clumped foliage and a thick, rooted trunk. The candidate is a sparse, thin bare tree with a greyscale ramp of only about 3-4 steps (white, light grey, mid grey, near-black). The dark outlines and branches are close to neutral black-grey with little tint. The trunk has a few birch-mark dots, but most of it is a narrow strip of flat white, and the canopy is mostly empty background with scattered twigs. Per-tile colour counts are low (about 3-5) compared with the reference's roughly 10 and above. It reads thinner and flatter than the references.
